packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-08 -- unverified image reading (blind first reader)

Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this fragment. I did nothing beyond the brief's rules (Read tool only on the brief, PROMPT.md and packet images; files opened by guessed sequential name image-NNN.jpg since directory listing was not permitted).

LAYOUT SURVEY (from image-001, reduced overview)
- image-001: whole small parchment strip on black, colour checker and scale. Strip roughly 5.5 cm wide x 11 cm tall, portrait orientation. A modern pencil shelfmark-type note along the top ("...Stams... 105..."-like, modern hand) in the upper blank area.
- Text is a single narrow block of writing at the left half of the strip, running from about one-quarter down to the bottom edge (approx. 25 visible lines). The text is cut at the left edge (line beginnings lost) and the right portion of the strip is blank parchment (margin or intercolumn), so this appears to be the right part of a column with its outer/inner margin to the right. Upper part of strip blank (top margin?). Bottom lines cut off.
- Small script, heavily abbreviated, Gothic textualis-type book hand, appears brown ink. No rubrics, initials or glosses visible at overview scale. Stains and holes (dark spots) mid-strip at right; a horizontal crease/fold around line 8-9.
- Interpretation (tentative): fragment of a scholastic/academic prose text in one column (or one column of two) cut down for binding.

TILE image-002 (top of strip; top margin + first ~10 text lines)
Observations: modern pencil note in top margin, upside down relative to the text? No - it reads left-to-right in the same orientation, roughly "Stams, Stb.(?) Frg.(?) 105 m" (modern, not transcribed further). Horizontal dry-point/plummet ruling lines run across the whole width, including the blank right part, so the blank area is ruled column space or margin beyond a vertical bounding line (a faint vertical line is visible just right of the text, around x=460). Text left edge cut: line beginnings lost. Lines 6-7 under a large brown stain; lines 8-10 increasingly faint, holes at line 9 in the margin.
Line numbering below counts text lines from the top of the image.

                 [reading "]i(m)al ro(nale) mor(ta)le est r(ationa)le" = (an)imal rationale mortale est rationale? -- tentative; superscript "le" over both "mor" and "r"]
image-002 l.4  ]assu(m)at(ur) au(tem) q(uo)d(?) ca(us)a(?) p(ri)ma(?) [?] er(?)ad(?)
                 [superscripts over several words; "assumatur autem quod" fairly likely, rest uncertain]

                 [again "animal rationale mortale est homo" pattern, tentative]

image-002 l.7  ]s(?) [illegible] fili(?) [illegible] p(er)?

image-002 l.9  ] et m(?) [faint - illegible]
image-002 l.10 ]ce(?) [illegible, very faint] [?]am(?)
Limitations: lines 6-10 stained/faded; I could not recover connected sense. The next tile should overlap these lines.

TILE image-003 (lower part of strip, to bottom edge)
Overlap: image-003 l.1 = image-002 l.8; l.2 = image-002 l.9; l.3 = image-002 l.10 (a sliver of image-002 l.7 is cut at the very top and not counted). So image-003 l.4 onward is new text. Total visible text lines on the face ~ image-002 l.1-10 + image-003 l.4-17 = 24 lines, the last cut at the bottom edge.
Observations: vertical bounding line visible just right of the text block (writing slightly crosses it on some lines); horizontal ruling continues across the blank right area. Some line-ends carry a vertical stroke "/" or "|" mid-line (l.13, l.15, l.16), probably punctuation/division strokes rather than column lines. A marginal word in the right blank area at l.11 with a caret-like mark above it: probably an addition/correction keyed to the text. Holes/ink spots in the right margin. Left edge of text cut throughout.

image-003 l.16 ]no(?) (ve)l sapie(n)tibus / (ve)l plu(r)ibus·   [superscript mark over "no"]
image-003 l.17 ]a(?)ct(?) [?] no(n)? (ve)l sapi(entibus)? (ve)l plu(ribus)?   [cut at bottom edge; superscript "ꝫ"/"z" above "sapi"]

Phrases read with reasonable confidence: "procedit exponibilis simpliciter" (l.6), "fiet conclusio ut" (l.7), "ad nos sequitur quod" (l.8), "non est exponibilis simpliciter non est exponibilis" (l.11), "et procedit non" (l.15), "vel sapientibus vel pluribus" (l.16), and on image-002 the repeated "(an)imal rationale mortale est rationale / ... rationale mortale est homo sequitur quod" (l.3, l.5).

LIMITATIONS
- Only one face seen so far (images 001-003). Left portion of every line is cut off, so no line is complete; connected sense across lines is limited.
- Lines image-002 l.6-10 / image-003 l.1-4 are stained and faded; mostly illegible.
- Many abbreviation expansions above are tentative (esp. "fare", "oz", "demo(n)...", "ca(us)a").
- No rubrics, initials, underlining or interlinear glosses seen; one marginal addition at image-003 l.11.
- A higher-contrast view of the stained band and the left (cut) edge would not recover line beginnings, which are physically lost.
(The limitations above refer to face 1, images 001-003.)

LAYOUT SURVEY, FACE 2 (image-004, reduced overview)
- Same strip, other face (approx. 5.5 x 11 cm). Text block occupies the RIGHT half of the strip, from about one-fifth down to the bottom edge, ~25 lines; the left half is blank (ruled?) margin with stains, holes and a vertical crease at the text's left boundary. So here line beginnings should be visible and line ends cut at the right edge (consistent with face 1, where line ends survive and beginnings are lost).
- A modern pencil note in the top margin, appearing upside down/rotated relative to the text (probably the same shelfmark note seen through or written on this side).
- A small green mark near the top right of the text block. Surface more abraded/patchy than face 1. Horizontal fold around line 6-7 with holes.

TILE image-005 (face 2, top: margin + first ~10 text lines)
Observations: modern pencil note in the top margin, upside down relative to the text, reading roughly "Stams, Stb., Frg. 105v" (so face 1 is probably the note's "r"; not further interpreted). A small green dot above the text near line 1, right side. Text block begins at a vertical line/crease about mid-strip; line beginnings are visible on this face, line ends cut at the right edge. Surface badly abraded and stained on lines 2-7; the left half of the strip is blank and stained.

Limitations: lines 2-7 are abraded to the point of near illegibility. Holes between l.7 and l.8 lie in the blank left margin, not in the text.

TILE image-006 (face 2, lower part to bottom edge)
Overlap: image-006 l.1 (partial, cut at top) = image-005 l.7; l.2 = image-005 l.8; l.3 = image-005 l.9; l.4 = image-005 l.10. New text from l.5. Face 2 therefore shows ~ image-005 l.1-10 + image-006 l.5-18 = 24 lines, the last cut at the bottom.
Observation on the letter group "eydua-/exdua-": on this tile it recurs as "ex duab(us)" (l.13) and the forms are consistent with "ex duabus"; I therefore re-express image-005 l.3 and l.8 as possibly "ex duabu[s]" / "ex duab(us) p(re)missis" (decided on letter shapes seen on this tile; image-005 is still in view).
Vertical bounding line visible at the left of the text block; horizontal ruling.

Phrases on face 2 read with reasonable confidence: "ex duabus premissis" (image-005 l.8 / image-006 l.2), "ergo omnis homo est risibilis" (l.6), "mortale est risibile" (l.8), "homo est animal rationale mortale" (l.9), "aut aliam premi[ssam]" (l.12), "nec ex duabus" (l.13), "et ex premissa" (l.14), "est quod non" (l.16), "aut aliam" (l.16).

OVERALL LIMITATIONS AND UNREAD AREAS
- Two faces, each a narrow strip of one column: face 1 (images 001-003) preserves line ends (beginnings cut); face 2 (images 004-006) preserves line beginnings (ends cut). Neither face gives a complete line.
- Unread/illegible: face 1 image-002 l.6-10 (stain), face 2 image-005 l.2-7 (abrasion) and scattered words on image-006 l.6-7, 10-11.
- Abbreviation expansions are tentative throughout; "sillo" read as possibly "sillo(gismus)" only from letters + superscript, not certain.
- No headings, rubrics, initials or underlining seen on either face. One marginal addition on face 1 (image-003 l.11).
- If a further pass is made, a raking-light or UV image of face 2 lines 2-7 and of the stained band on face 1 would be the most useful additional views.
